text: The wilderness and the parched land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.

versions.text: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.
versions.explanation: Minor: "dry land" can suggest land as opposed to sea (as in Genesis 1); "parched land" renders צִיָּה more precisely and reads well aloud.

text: It will burst into bloom and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon is given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands, steady the buckling knees.
Say to those with anxious hearts: Be strong, do not fear! Look, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God; he will come and save you.
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy. For water will break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground bubbling springs. In the haunt where jackals lie down, there will be grass, with reeds and rushes.

versions.text: The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground bubbling springs. In the haunt where jackals lay, there will be grass, with reeds and rushes.
versions.explanation: "where jackals lay" uses an odd past tense; the sense is their resting place. Consider "In the haunt where jackals lie down" for tense consistency with the surrounding future-tense verbs.

versions.text: In the haunt where jackals lay, there will be grass, with reeds and rushes growing.
versions.explanation: The entire first half of the verse is missing: וְהָיָה הַשָּׁרָב לַאֲגַם וְצִמָּאוֹן לְמַבּוּעֵי מָיִם ("the burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground bubbling springs"). This clause has been restored from the earlier version. Additionally, "lay" is corrected to "lie down" for tense consistency with the surrounding future-tense verbs (the point of the earlier revision note), and the added word "growing", which has no counterpart in the Hebrew, is removed.

text: And a highway will be there, a road, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it; it is for those who walk the way, and fools will not go astray.

versions.text: And a highway will be there, a road, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it; it belongs to the one who walks that way, and fools will not stray onto it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew לֹא יִתְעוּ means simply "will not go astray/lose their way"; "stray onto it" reverses the sense, implying fools are kept off the road rather than that travelers on it cannot lose their way. Also לָמוֹ is plural, so "for those who walk" is closer than the singular.

text: No lion will be there, no ravenous beast will go up on it; none will be found there. But the redeemed will walk it.
The ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with singing, everlasting joy upon their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
